intro.title: Generic List<T>
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable Vue component that displays a list of items of any type, such as a list of names, numbers, or products. You will learn about Vue's built-in reactivity system and how to use props to pass data into components. The core programming concept is generics, which allows your component to work with different data types without rewriting code. You'll use Vue's template syntax to render the list and practice defining props with type validation to make your component flexible and type-safe.
intro.usecase: Generic List<T> patterns appear throughout modern web applications where developers need to handle collections of data with consistent type safety. In Vue applications, you'll use these patterns when building data tables in admin dashboards, product lists in e-commerce interfaces, or user selection components in forms. This approach ensures your components work reliably with different data types—whether displaying customer records, inventory items, or notification messages—while maintaining clean, reusable code. Mastering generics helps you create flexible list components that adapt to various data structures without sacrificing type checking or code clarity.
